title: 叠加定理：两台电源分别作用，再相加
summary: 9 V 和 5 V 两台电源一起驱动 R3。用开关把电源换成导线，分别测、再一起测：电流正好相加，功率却不行。
concepts: zeroing a voltage source = short 电压源置零 = 短路
power is not superposable 功率不能叠加
description: 线性电路里，几个独立源一起作用产生的电流或电压，等于每个源单独作用（其他电压源换成导线）时的结果之和。功率不能这样叠加。

cards.title: 三次读数，找找关系
text: 照目标电路图搭：**两台稳压电源**，`9 V` 和 `5 V`，两条蓝轨连起来当 GND。每个开关的 **a** 侧接电源 +，**b** 侧接 GND。
**S1 → b，S2 → a**：再读一次。然后**两个都拨到 a**：读第三次。
第三个读数和前两个有什么关系？

cards.title: 各推各的，推力相加
text: - 开关拨到 **b**，电阻的那一端就接到了 GND：电源被换成了**一根导线**（0 V）。这就是“把电压源置零”——是短路，**不是**把线拔掉悬空。
- 只由电阻和电源组成的电路里，每个电源推动 R3 里的电流时，都好像另一个电源只是那根导线。一起作用时，推力直接相加：
![](fig:alone)
- 量之前想一想：R3 的**功率**也能这样相加吗？

cards.title: 三种组合，逐一读数
text: - 两个都在 a 时，再用万用表**测 N 对 GND 的电压**。
- 电路检查通过后填测量题。最后一题把电流平方，算功率。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **叠加定理**：线性电路里，几个电源产生的电流、电压可以相加。
- 置零：电压源换成**导线**，电流源换成**断开**。
- 坑：LED、二极管不是线性元件。路上有一颗，加法就不灵了。

caption.text: 只有 V1 作用：S2 拨到 b，V2 被换成一根导线，R2 的那一端直接接 GND。

i18n.en: V1 alone: S2 on b replaces V2 with a wire, so R2's end goes straight to GND.

en.title: Superposition: one source at a time, then add
en.summary: A 9 V and a 5 V supply drive R3 together. Swap a supply for a wire with a switch, measure each alone and then both: the currents add up — the power does not.
concepts: zeroing a voltage source = short circuit
en.description: In a linear circuit the current or voltage produced by several independent sources together is the sum of what each produces alone (with the other voltage sources replaced by wires). Power does not add this way.
en.compare:
**Compare**: the bottom is 1 + 0.4545 + 0.3030 = 1.7576 mS.
- Only V1 (S1 → a, S2 → b): V_N = 9 / 1.7576 ≈ **5.12 V**, I3 ≈ **1.55 mA**.
- Only V2 (S1 → b, S2 → a): V_N = 2.273 / 1.7576 ≈ **1.29 V**, I3 ≈ **0.39 mA**.
- Both (a, a): V_N ≈ **6.41 V**, I3 ≈ **1.94 mA** = 1.55 + 0.39 ✔.

If the readings don't fit, first make sure the switch of the source you turned off is on b (GND), not left open.

**Power does not add**: alone, 1.55² × 3.3 ≈ 7.9 mW and 0.39² × 3.3 ≈ 0.5 mW, together 8.4 mW; with both on it is 1.94² × 3.3 ≈ 12.5 mW.

Only V2 (S1 → b, S2 → a): AM1 reading I3″
Both on (a, a): AM1 reading I3
measurements.explain: I3 = I3′ + I3″ ≈ 1.55 + 0.39 = 1.94 mA: superposition holds.

measurements.ask: Square your three currents for R3's power P = I²R: I3′²R + I3″²R compared with I3²R is
measurements.explain: ≈ 7.9 + 0.5 = 8.4 mW, but 1.94² × 3.3 ≈ 12.5 mW. (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab; the extra 2ab is the gap. Power goes with the square of the current, so it does not superpose.

cards.title: Three readings — spot the pattern
text: Build it from the target schematic: **two bench supplies**, `9 V` and `5 V`, with their blue rails joined as GND. Each switch has its **a** side on a supply's + and its **b** side on GND.
**S1 → a, S2 → b**: read the ammeter **AM1**.
**S1 → b, S2 → a**: read AM1 again. Then **both on a**: read it a third time.
How does the third reading relate to the first two?

cards.title: Each source pushes on its own; the pushes add
text: - With a switch on **b**, its end of the resistor goes to GND: the supply is replaced by **a plain wire** (0 V). That is what "turning a voltage source off" means — a short, **not** an open lead.
- In a circuit made of resistors and sources, each source pushes current through R3 as if the other were that wire. Together, the pushes simply add:
![](fig:alone)
- To predict each part, use the node voltage from 2.2: with only V1, $V_N' = \frac{V_1/R_1}{1/R_1 + 1/R_2 + 1/R_3}$. The bottom is $1 + 0.4545 + 0.3030 = 1.758$ mS. Do the same for V2 alone.
- Before you measure: will the **power** in R3 add the same way?

cards.title: Three settings, one by one
text: - **S1 → a, S2 → b** (only V1), **S1 → b, S2 → a** (only V2), **both → a**: read AM1 each time.
- With both on a, also **measure N to GND** with the multimeter.
- Once the circuit check passes, fill in the questions. The last one squares your currents to get the power.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **Superposition**: in a linear circuit, currents and voltages from several sources add up.
- Turning a source off: a voltage source becomes a **wire**, a current source becomes an **open** gap.
- **Power does not superpose**: $P = I^2R$ and $(a + b)^2 ≠ a^2 + b^2$.
- Pitfall: an LED or a diode is not linear. Put one in the path and the sums stop working.
